items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: I don’t care if you want to write a piece about if you’re Charles Ives and you want to write the Housatonic at Stockbridge

ctx.x: Yes. It is happy. There doesn’t have to be dominant chords in it. It’s interesting. You write a piece that feels as if it moves forward and doesn’t have any tritones hidden in it but it’s not really — they don’t do the same thing that a dominant chord does. Yeah, I liked the feeling of Bill’s piece walking up and I thought oh I like the feeling of that, let

me do my own version of that. So my pieces are, they come from other musical ideas that I’ve heard. And that’s just me. I don’t care if you want to write a piece about if you’re Charles Ives and you want to write the Housatonic at Stockbridge I know Stockbridge and the Housatonic River very well and I understand it’s very nice. But I can’t paint a picture of that in music. I can take a photograph and that’s — my music is — I don’t maintain that that’s how everyone should do it, that’s just how my mind works.

Have you ever written something and then only to find out that someone already wrote it? What you wrote was so close to something else that you realized that you were sort of channeling something else?
